summary: POC request: how to pin a known-good runtime hardware profile pack version (avoid perf changes during evaluation)
description:
Customer asks how to keep inference performance stable during a Dedicated POC while Redwood rolls out the new versioned hardware tuning profiles pack.

Issue summary
- Customer is evaluating Dedicated (H100) and is seeing small performance variability week-over-week.
- They want to pin to a known-good profile pack version for the duration of the POC, and understand how/when it can be updated.

Customer ask (paraphrased)
- "Can we pin the hardware performance profile to whatever you consider stable today, and only change it with our approval?"

Impact
- Risk of evaluation noise / perceived regression if default profile changes in Redwood Hosted/Dedicated rollout.

Environment
- Dedicated cluster (H100), region us-east
- Runtime train: 1.22.x (per customer email)
- Workload: mixed prompt lengths, streaming enabled

Questions to answer
1) Is profile pack pinning supported for Dedicated?
2) What is the recommended pin mechanism?
3) What guardrails apply (unsupported combos, rollback behavior)?

Attachments / logs
- None provided. Customer is asking for procedure + best practice.

Support notes
- This ticket is intended as a procedural/how-to response. If the customer also wants a performance review, route to CS/SA after pin is applied.
comments: 2026-02-19 09:12 (Kira Thompson, Support) — Created from customer email via CS. Customer wants to avoid perf shifts during Dedicated POC; asking how to pin a known-good hardware profile version. Looping in Runtime config owner for authoritative guidance (cc Ethan Park).

2026-02-19 10:03 (Ethan Park, Eng - Platform/Runtime Config) — Confirmed: pinning profile pack version is supported for Dedicated via the per-deployment runtime config override (profile_version). Guardrails apply: only allow versions that are compatible with detected GPU SKU + driver/CUDA baseline; unsafe pins are rejected with an audit log entry. This requires a rolling restart of the runtime pods to take effect.

2026-02-19 10:15 (Kira Thompson, Support) — Draft response to customer:
- Yes, we can pin profile pack version for Dedicated for the duration of your POC.
- We recommend pinning at the deployment level (not per-request), so all replicas in the pool run the same tuning defaults.
- We can also rollback quickly by returning to the previous pinned version.

Ethan: what version should we recommend as “known-good” today for H100? (Assuming current stable is 1.22 profile pack v1.0.x?)

2026-02-19 11:02 (Ethan Park) — For H100 Dedicated in us-east, recommend pinning to profile pack version "1.0.3" (current stable; matches our Hosted canary graduation). If they’re already on it, pinning will simply make future defaults non-impacting.

What to tell customer:
- We’ll set profile_version=1.0.3 and enable “customer approval required” for changes during POC.
- Any future change would be coordinated (we’ll propose an update window + share expected behavior deltas).

Internal: we should add a short public-facing Dedicated FAQ entry on profile pinning vs default rollouts (doc gap).

2026-02-19 12:20 (Kira Thompson, Support → Customer) — Shared guidance:
1) We can pin your Dedicated deployment to a specific tuning profile pack version (recommended for POCs where repeatability matters).
2) We will pin you to profile pack version 1.0.3 (our current stable for H100).
3) This is a deployment-level setting; it applies to all replicas in the pool and remains in place until we change it with you.
4) Guardrails: profile pins are validated against your hardware/driver baseline; if an incompatible combination is detected, the platform blocks the change and we’ll coordinate next steps.
5) Rollback: if needed, we can revert to the prior pinned version; we’ll also include the active profile info in our debug bundle (/health) for transparency.

Asked customer to confirm a maintenance window for a rolling restart (no downtime expected; brief capacity reduction during restart).
2026-02-20 08:41 (Customer) — Confirmed. Please pin to 1.0.3 and keep it stable for the rest of the POC. Maintenance window OK: 18:00–20:00 ET.

2026-02-20 09:10 (Rafael Mendes, SRE) — Scheduled change for customer window. Will apply config override and monitor: p95/p99 latency, error rate, scheduler_queue_ms, kernel fallback counters. If any unexpected tail latency, rollback to previous profile version immediately.

2026-02-20 19:02 (Rafael Mendes, SRE) — Change executed: set profile_version=1.0.3 on customer Dedicated deployment; rolling restart completed. Post-change check (30 min): error rate flat, p95 stable, p99 slightly improved (~3–5%). No kernel fallback spikes. Marking as resolved pending next-business-day confirmation from customer.

2026-02-24 09:37 (Kira Thompson, Support) — Customer confirmed stability during their next test run; no further requests. Closing ticket.

Follow-up: opening doc task for Dedicated profile pinning FAQ + how to verify active profile_version in debug bundle.
resolution: Pinned customer Dedicated deployment to hardware tuning profile pack version 1.0.3 for duration of POC (deployment-level profile_version override with compatibility guardrails). Completed rolling restart in agreed window and verified stability via SRE monitoring. Opened follow-up documentation task to clarify pinning procedure and verification steps for Dedicated customers.
